instagram.caption: A Boulder bartender with eight years behind the bar says the biggest change he's seen isn't the chaos. It's that people can't stay focused long enough to order, get, and pay for one drink. From our Longmont Locals chat with the Longmont Writer's Group. Full episode link in bio.

facebook.post: Eight years tending bar at the Sundowner on Pearl Street, and one change stands out to this bartender: attention spans. He says customers order, get distracted, turn around, and he practically has to beg them to finish the transaction. It came up on this week's Longmont Locals with Andrea Mann and Matt Crutchfield of the Longmont Writer's Group, in a bigger conversation about why focus (and reading) feels harder than ever. Have you noticed this in your own life, or behind a counter of your own?

bluesky.post: A Boulder bartender says the biggest change in eight years: people can't keep their attention long enough to finish ordering a single drink.

discord.message: New clip from Longmont Locals with the Longmont Writer's Group: a story about a Sundowner bartender who says customers can't stay focused through ordering one drink anymore. Funny and a little alarming. Curious what y'all think, are we all this distracted?

instagram.caption: "Hello, my name is Andrea. I haven't written in three weeks." Turns out the Longmont Writer's Group is part support group, part accountability crew. Andrea Mann and Matt Crutchfield explain on Longmont Locals. Full episode link in bio. ✍️

facebook.post: Is a writers group basically AA for writers? According to Andrea Mann and Matt Crutchfield of the Longmont Writer's Group, that's not too far off. There's a lot of venting, a lot of getting back on the wagon, and plenty of room for people who haven't been on the wagon yet: folks who dabbled in creative writing in high school, built a world they never finished, and want to pick it back up. By the end of the clip, the group even has a name for it: Authors Anonymous. Have you ever had a creative project you wanted to come back to?

bluesky.post: "Hello, my name is Andrea. I haven't written in three weeks." The Longmont Writer's Group, aka Authors Anonymous.

discord.message: Clip up from this week's Longmont Locals: Andrea Mann and Matt Crutchfield on how the Longmont Writer's Group works like AA for writers (Authors Anonymous, as one text put it). If you've been sitting on a half-finished story, this one's for you.

instagram.caption: Biggest threat to writing right now? Bring up AI at the Longmont Writer's Group and the knives come out. Plus why reading itself is slipping. From Longmont Locals, full episode link in bio.

facebook.post: We asked our guests from the Longmont Writer's Group what they see as the new threats to writing. AI came up first, and as one of them put it, when you mention AI in the writers group, the knives come out. The other worry? Reading in general, and the time and intentional effort it takes, whether that's a physical book or an audiobook. It's a sharp moment from this week's Longmont Locals with Andrea Mann and Matt Crutchfield. Where do you land on AI in creative work?

bluesky.post: "When you mention AI in the writers group, the knives come out." Local writers on what's threatening the craft.

discord.message: Spicy one from Longmont Locals: the Longmont Writer's Group on AI and writing (the knives come out) and why they think our culture is drifting away from reading. Curious what y'all think about this one.

instagram.caption: Stephen King's "kill your darlings" is writing advice. It turns out it's pretty good life advice too. If you think it's God's gift to the world, question it. From Longmont Locals with the Longmont Writer's Group, full episode link in bio.

facebook.post: "Kill your darlings" is one of Stephen King's big rules: don't keep something just because you like it, look for the best thing. Add in the rejection letter that told him final draft equals first draft minus 10%, and you've got a pretty brutal editing philosophy. On this week's Longmont Locals with Andrea Mann and Matt Crutchfield, the conversation turned to how well it works outside of writing, for anything you're building or creating in your life. What's a darling you've had to let go of?

bluesky.post: Final draft equals first draft minus 10%. Kill your darlings works on a lot more than writing.

discord.message: New clip: Stephen King's "kill your darlings" and the minus 10% rule, and how the Longmont Writer's Group crew thinks it applies to life in general. From this week's Longmont Locals. Anyone actually follow the 10% rule?

instagram.caption: January Coffee's owners looked at that storefront years ago and thought it would make a great coffee shop. Then John Imig ended up setting up its coffee bar for Landline back in 2021. Now it's theirs. ☕ Full Longmont Locals episode link in bio.

facebook.post: Here's a sweet bit of Longmont business news. The couple behind January Coffee live in Longmont and eyed this storefront years ago when it was for sale. Landline moved in instead, and while consulting for Ozo, John Imig actually set up Landline's coffee bar himself in 2021. Fast forward five years, and January Coffee is the one landing in the space, opening (fittingly) in January. It's from the top of this week's Longmont Locals. Will you be stopping by when they open?

bluesky.post: January Coffee's owner set up the coffee bar in that Longmont space back in 2021, for Landline. Five years later it's his. And yes, they open in January.

discord.message: Local news clip from this week's Longmont Locals: the serendipitous story of how January Coffee ended up in the old Landline space, where John Imig built the coffee bar years ago. Bonus question from the crew: will they be open Sundays?
